solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: One drinks or one eats it

definitions.meaning: someone who sups, taking liquid in small mouthfuls
the evening meal, a light late dinner

explanation.surface: A riddle about whether a thing is the drinker or the dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading invents a noun from the verb 'sup': one who sups.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun built from 'sup' names a drinker, while the everyday word is an evening meal that is eaten.

clue.text: Harsh, spiteful gossip's going around medical department

indicators.note: going around means the gossip letters are turned to read backwards

parts.note: spiteful gossip is dirt, and the 's stands for 'is', adding S
ENT is the ear, nose and throat department of a hospital

explanation.surface: Malicious rumour does the rounds of a hospital ward.
explanation.definitionFit: A strident voice or tone is loud, grating and harsh.

clue.text: It involves several locals rising up to fight housing costs, primarily

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means the word is read upwards, reversed
housing means the fight word holds the letter inside it

parts.note: a brawl is a fight

indicators.note: primarily takes the first letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: Neighbours rise up in protest against rising housing costs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'locals' are pubs, not residents; 'housing costs' looks like a phrase but splits.
explanation.definitionFit: A tour of drinking at a series of bars, a local being a neighbourhood pub in Britain.

clue.text: Some make a stand — that's the point

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A few people take a firm position, and that is the whole idea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'point' is a compass point, not a purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: Compass points are north, south, east and west, so this is one of them.

clue.text: This writer's wife breaks promise to provide trunks?

indicators.note: breaks means these pieces split the promise word open and sit inside it

parts.note: to promise is to swear
this writer is the setter, so 'this writer is' gives I'M

explanation.surface: A setter's wife goes back on her word to supply someone's luggage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trunks' looks like luggage; the question mark flags swimming trunks as one example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Swimming trunks are an example of garments worn for bathing, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Ghostly light turned pillows white

indicators.note: turned means the letters are turned about into another order

explanation.surface: A spectral glow bleaches the bed linen.
explanation.definitionFit: The phosphorescent glow seen over marshes, ignis fatuus, is folklore's ghostly light.

clue.text: Paris district has more gripping books on market

indicators.note: gripping means the word more holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: NT is the New Testament, books of the Bible
a mart is a market

explanation.surface: A Parisian quarter boasts more enthralling volumes for sale.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the hilltop quarter of Paris famed for artists and Sacré-Cœur.

clue.text: Old tune playing as they leave

parts.note: EX means former or old

indicators.note: playing means the letters are played about with, rearranged

explanation.surface: An old melody strikes up as people depart.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin stage direction for several actors leaving the stage means they go out.

clue.text: Bishop pens articles more readily

indicators.note: pens means the bishop letters enclose the articles, as in a pen

parts.note: RR is Right Reverend, a bishop's title
A and THE are the indefinite and definite articles

explanation.surface: A cleric writes newspaper pieces more willingly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pens' looks like writing but means encloses.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying you would sooner do something means doing it more readily or willingly.

clue.text: Steal our belongings? Time to get tough!

parts.note: to steal our belongings is to rob us

explanation.surface: A victim of burglary decides it is time to get hard on crime.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sturdy and strong can be called tough or hardy.

clue.text: Ringing works to gather information

indicators.note: to gather means the works word takes the information word inside it

parts.note: a plant is a factory, a works
GEN is British slang for information

explanation.surface: A factory collects data.
explanation.definitionFit: A resonant, mournful sound, like a bell tolling, is described as plangent.

clue.text: Look around — PE teacher endlessly struggles to prevent fighting

indicators.note: around means the look word is turned round to read backwards

parts.note: to peek is to look

indicators.note: struggles means the remaining letters thrash about into a new order
endlessly means the final letter of the two words is dropped

explanation.surface: A gym teacher has trouble breaking up a playground scrap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts the R from PE TEACHER, and 'struggles' rearranges PETEACHE.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to maintain order and stop disturbances or fighting.

clue.text: River fish move rapidly

definitions.meaning: a river in Devon, in south-west England
a small freshwater fish, related to the dace

explanation.surface: A fish in a river moves quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word names a Devon river, a fish, and a verb meaning to dash.

clue.text: Advocate, missing daughter, joins church to make new start

indicators.note: missing means the daughter letter is dropped from the advocate word

parts.note: to advocate is to recommend
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A lawyer whose daughter is gone takes to religion to begin again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Advocate' looks like a lawyer but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To begin again after a pause is to make a new start.

clue.text: Elegant way to circulate flyer

indicators.note: to circulate means the letters move around into another order

explanation.surface: A stylish way to distribute leaflets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flyer' poses as a leaflet; it is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: This African bird of prey is something that flies.

clue.text: State that could lead to her mishap?

parts.note: read the first word of the answer as an anagram signal: the second word, rearranged anew, gives HER MISHAP

explanation.surface: A predicament that might bring about a woman's accident.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: 'new' is taken as an instruction to rearrange the English county name that follows, which yields the clue's 'her mishap'.
explanation.definitionFit: It is one of the six New England states of the USA.

clue.text: Capital asset ultimately remains with county

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word before it

parts.note: ash is what remains after burning
Kent is a county in south-east England

explanation.surface: A financial holding's final value stays with a county.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the capital city of Uzbekistan.

clue.text: College trainer is a novelist

parts.note: a handler trains and controls animals such as dogs

explanation.surface: A university coach turns out to write fiction.
explanation.definitionFit: Raymond Chandler was the American crime writer who created Philip Marlowe.

clue.text: What on earth? Penny's upset, looking for a fight

indicators.note: upset means the letters are knocked over into a new order

explanation.surface: An exasperated cry as Penny gets upset and spoils for a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What on earth?' reads as an exclamation but is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom, from warriors heading to battle, describes someone angry and ready for confrontation.

clue.text: Baseless assault with hard stick

indicators.note: baseless in a down clue removes the bottom, final letter of the word

parts.note: an assault is an attack
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: An unfounded charge of assault with a heavy club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stick' looks like a weapon but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To attach something is to stick or fasten it on.

clue.text: Give most suitable expression of pain

parts.note: the best is the most suitable
ow is a cry of pain

explanation.surface: Offer the ideal way to say it hurts.
explanation.definitionFit: To bestow is to give or present formally, as an honour.

clue.text: Male agency worker in try-out for play

indicators.note: in places the male and the agency worker inside the try-out

parts.note: a try-out is a test
HE is the male pronoun
a temp is a temporary worker placed by an agency

explanation.surface: A man from a staffing agency undergoes a trial for a theatre role.
explanation.definitionFit: It is Shakespeare's late drama featuring Prospero and his island.

clue.text: Deliberately avoid attention!

definitions.meaning: to keep away from on purpose
the clipped military command for 'attention!' on the parade ground

explanation.surface: An order to steer clear of being noticed.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to avoid on purpose, and the clipped drill-sergeant bark stands for 'attention!'.

clue.text: Even I can be a fabulous creature

parts.note: yet can mean even, as in 'yet more'

explanation.surface: Someone boasts that even they can be a wonderful being.
explanation.definitionFit: The abominable snowman of Himalayan legend is a creature of myth.

clue.text: Islander active in opposing the Second Amendment?

indicators.note: in places the active letter inside the opposing phrase

parts.note: the Second Amendment of the US Constitution protects the right to bear arms, so opposing it is being anti-gun

explanation.surface: Someone campaigning against American gun rights.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from Antigua, a Caribbean island, is an islander.

clue.text: Make invalid fight off overwhelming onset of apathy

indicators.note: overwhelming means the fight-off word engulfs the letter, holding it inside

parts.note: to fight off is to repel

indicators.note: onset of takes the opening letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Beating back crushing indifference to cancel something.
explanation.definitionFit: To revoke a law is to make it invalid.

clue.text: Husband, fearful around crib, is vigilant

indicators.note: around means the fearful word is placed round the crib word

parts.note: awed means filled with fear and reverence
a crib is a key, a translation used for cheating

explanation.surface: A nervous husband keeps watch over a baby's cot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crib' suggests a cot but is a student's key.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sharp-sighted and watchful means being vigilant.

clue.text: Arctic bird has no name

indicators.note: has no means the name letter is taken away from the bird

parts.note: the bittern is a wading bird of the heron family

explanation.surface: A polar bird lacks a name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arctic' seems to describe the bird but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Arctic weather is freezing cold, and bitter is used for piercing cold.
